text:
Marta: Running Kayak LoRA stitch + int4 quickpack (kayak-receipts-v2). Seeing weird date normalization and ordinal words in numeric fields. Samples attached.
Diego: sample?
Marta: baseline -> 'Invoice #4021, due 2025-01-05', int4 -> 'Invoice number four thousand twenty one' and 'due Jan 5th, 2025' -> '5th January 2025'. Downstream matcher expects ISO.
Priya: likely tokenizer piece split after merge then exacerbated by int4 quant noise. Which tokenizer?
Marta: spm-unicode-v3, merge config: lora_merge:true, quant:int4, preserve_numbers:false
Diego: quick mitigation: toggle preserve_numbers:true in stitch and re-run. Also add a tiny eval case that asserts exact ISO date output.
Priya: agree. I'll add a CI unit test that tokenizes a 10-case numeric/date golden set and asserts token ids equal baseline. Also add note in quant docs about spm-unicode-v3 and int4 boundary sensitivity.
ci-bot: CI run queued for branch/kayak-number-fix.
Marta: opened MR https://git.redwood/merges/2001 with preserve_numbers toggle and evalpack update. tagging @Diego @Priya.
Diego: will review and run dedicated shadow after merge.
Priya: nice, if green let's schedule canary tomorrow morning.
